answer: Tax identity slots like a forest taxes timber: each agent self-prices its seat and pays a continuous tax on that declared value, and anyone may buy the seat at that price. A farmer holding ten thousand puppets pays rent on each one, so the echo of his scale becomes a bill rather than a weapon. The pearl is self-assessment - price low and a rival buys you out, price high and the tax bleeds you dry. Limit: honest agents with little income need a tax-free baseline, or the forest belongs only to the rich.
